newsitem.title: USA: Papers show file gathering was error - White House.
newsitem.headline: Papers show file gathering was error - White House.

text.p: The White House released documents Wednesday that it said proved President Clinton's insistence that the collection of confidential FBI reports on Republicans was simply a bureaucratic blunder.

Officials said the documents showed White House security official Anthony Marceca was working from inaccurate lists produced by the Secret Service when he obtained from the FBI secret background investigations on hundreds of Republicans from the administrations of Ronald Reagan and George Bush.

A White House associate counsel, Mark Fabiani, released a thick stack of papers that he said constituted the faulty Secret Service lists Marceca was using. He said the White House would have released them sooner but they had been in the custody of Kenneth Starr, the independent counsel investigating cases involving Clinton and his wife, Hillary.

"These newly revealed Secret Service lists support what the White House has said all along about the FBI files matter: The files were mistakenly sought as the result of a bureaucratic blunder," Fabiani said.
Republicans have charged that in collecting the files on Republicans, the White House was compiling an "enemies list" and committed an extreme violation of privacy.

The House Government Reform and Oversight Committee adopted an interim report on the FBI files case Tuesday and called for a top FBI official to resign. It accused the White House of trying to politicize the bureau.

Republicans reject Clinton's explanation that aides sought files on the wrong people in the course of approving people for regular access to the White House because the Secret Service provided lists with people who no longer worked there.

Sen. Orrin Hatch of Utah, chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee, said he was not convinced the White House was innocent. He said the committee had evidence that Marceca, knowing the lists were inaccurate, requested from the FBI background reports on Republicans he knew no longer worked at the White House.

"Perhaps this will shed some light," he told CNN, referring to the newly released documents. Hatch's committee was holding a hearing to investigate the files case further, with testimony from witnesses including the White House's former personnel security chief, Craig Livingstone.
The lists were in two boxes of documents the White House turned over to the FBI in June when it was disclosed that Marceca, who worked for Livingstone, had collected the files.
Fabiani said the White House had sought their return to prove its point that the lists were faulty but the FBI had turned them over to Starr's investigators.

When Starr was asked to return them, the White House was told they would be sent back "at such time when disclosure of the documents would not hinder or impede our investigation." Deputy independent counsel John Bates returned the lists Tuesday, saying in a letter that "we believe that time has been reached."

Fabiani said the release of the lists undermined the Republicans' argument by proving the Secret Service produced them in June 1993 -- months after Clinton took office. This would mean the Secret Service was mistakenly giving the White House names of people who no longer worked there, he said.
"Republicans said it was an enemies list, but we said it was an older list used to do searches for FBI files," he said.
